question.problem:
Consider a curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s.$ Find the radius of curvature of $r(s)$ at an arbitrary point knowing that its unit tangent vector $T(s)$ is given by

$$
T(s)=\frac{1}{2}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{8}),\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{8}),\,\sqrt{3}⟩.
$$
question.worked_solution:
Since the curve $r(s)$ and its unit tangent vector $T(s)$ are both parametrized by arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the radius of curvature:

$$
R(s)=\frac{1}{κ(s)}=\frac{1}{‖{T}^{′}(s)‖}
$$

We differentiate $T(s)$ with respect to $s$ and calculate its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(s) & =\frac{1}{2}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{8})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{8})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\sqrt{3})⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨-\frac{1}{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{8}),\,-\frac{1}{8}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{8}),\,0⟩ \\  & =-\frac{1}{16}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{8}),\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{8}),\,0⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(s)‖ & =\frac{1}{16}\cdot \sqrt{{(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{8}))}^{2}+{(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{8}))}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{16}\cdot \sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{s}{8})+{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{s}{8})} \\  & =\frac{1}{16}\cdot \sqrt{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{16}\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{1}{16}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of curvature is

$$
R(s)=\frac{1}{‖{T}^{′}(s)‖}=\frac{1}{(\frac{1}{16})}=16.
$$
